paper_metadata.title: Synergistic grain boundary engineering for achieving strength-ductility balance in ultrafine-grained high-Cr-bearing multicomponent alloys

evidence.quote: a multi-step thermomechanical process is employed to regulate discontinuous dynamic recrystallization (DDRX) and static recrystallization, achieving an ultrafine-grained microstructure. However, the mechanical properties of high-Cr-bearing alloys are often compromised by brittle Cr-rich precipitates at grain boundaries (GBs), leading to severe embrittlement.
Co-Cr-Ni-Al-Ti alloy system
Previous studies have demonstrated that the solid-solution strengthening contribution of the Co-Cr-Ni-Al-Ti alloy system is relatively small ( ≈ 21.2 MPa) ( Liu et al., 2023 ).
a multi-step thermomechanical process was proposed to manipulate the sizes and distributions of fcc grains and GB precipitations in high-Cr-bearing multicomponent alloys

In our case, since a large amount of Ni, Cr, Al, and Ti is diffused out from the matrix to form submicron L1 2 and σ particles as observed, a low solid solution strengthening contribution should be obtained.
